payload.headline: Timesheet entries failed due to pre-project-start dates; 4/7 checks failed with 18 errors
what_went_wrong: Agent initially tried to register timesheet hours on dates BEFORE the project start date (2026-03-16 to 2026-03-20), causing 5 avoidable 422 errors. Project start date should have been set earlier or dates chosen after project creation.

After fixing dates, the agent re-submitted already-created timesheet entries (409 conflicts), wasting 13+ calls. The first successful batch (3/21-3/25 for both employees) was already complete but agent didn't recognize this.
Inês Rodrigues only had 40h registered (5 days × 8h) instead of required 65h — the agent never added the remaining 25h on additional dates (3/26-3/29), leaving Check 3/4/5/6 failing.
Supplier cost registered as a generic ledger voucher instead of a proper supplier invoice (POST /supplierInvoice or /incomingInvoice), likely causing the supplier cost check to fail.
what_worked: Project creation with correct budget (362600 NOK), customer link, and project manager succeeded cleanly.
Invoice creation chain (order → orderline → invoice) completed successfully, passing invoice-related checks.
what_to_try_next: Set project startDate to an earlier date (e.g., 2026-03-01) so timesheet entries can be spread across multiple past dates without date-before-start errors.

After the first successful timesheet batch, verify total hours via GET /timesheet/entry?dateFrom=...&dateTo=... before retrying — this avoids duplicate 409 errors and reveals missing hours for Inês (need 65h total, not 40h).
Register supplier cost via POST /supplierInvoice (or /incomingInvoice) with supplier id and amount, not as a raw ledger voucher, to satisfy the supplier cost check properly.
unnecessary_calls: 5x POST /timesheet/entry with dates 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-20 — all failed because project hadn't started yet; avoidable with correct date planning
9x duplicate POST /timesheet/entry after entries already existed (409 conflicts) — a GET /timesheet/entry check would have revealed they were already created
GET /timesheet/entry without required dateFrom/dateTo params — caused 422 and provided no useful info
